summary: Created one sovereign small-drone and trusted-component supply-chain idea. Funded EU and UK demand plus US trusted-supplier policy support recurring procurement, while component dependence, commoditisation, civil regulation, and margin conversion remain unresolved. Enqueued one bounded Parrot review; no relationship or strategy was created.

evidence.source: European Commission EU-Ukraine Drone Alliance launch
evidence.claim: The Commission launched an 18-member alliance to support joint ventures and accelerate EU-Ukrainian drone and counter-drone production.

evidence.source: European External Action Service Drone Deal
evidence.claim: The EU disbursed EUR 1 billion for Ukrainian drone capabilities and agreed to promote joint EU-Ukraine production by the end of 2026.

evidence.source: UK Ministry of Defence 2026 drone packages
evidence.claim: The UK announced at least 120,000 drones in April and funding for 150,000 Ukrainian-produced drones in June.
US policy directs agencies to prioritize US-manufactured drones, secure component supply chains, and expand access to trusted Blue UAS products.
Standard small-UAS operations generally still require visual line of sight, constraining routine advanced civil deployment.

daily_report_items: Researched sovereign small-drone supply chains: funded demand and trusted-supplier policy are real, but localization, unit economics, regulation, and margins block a strategy; queued Parrot research.
